can_do_statement: Can use 'It' + 'be' + noun + 'that' clause for focus.

ontology.mental_model: Highlighting a specific entity in discourse by placing it in a cleft structure
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'It is X that/who...' to emphasize the importance of X.

positives: It was Paul who stole the money.
It is this silence that gives me the impression of togetherness.
negatives: It is clear that he is absolutely right.
I know the man who is standing there.

can_do_statement: Can use more than one fixed expression in the front position for added focus.

ontology.mental_model: Stacking discourse markers for heavy emphasis at the beginning of a sentence
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use multiple fixed expressions like 'All in all, taking everything into account' to strongly frame your point.

positives: All in all, taking everything into account, it was a great experience.
All in all, taking everything into account, we decided to stay.
negatives: All in all it was quite good.
Taking everything into account, it was fine.

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative form with 'will'.

ontology.mental_model: Visualizing an action in progress at a point in the future
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'will be -ing' to describe an ongoing action in the future.

positives: I'll be waiting for you at the station.
We will be starting at noon.
negatives: I will be there on time.
She is waiting for you now.

can_do_statement: Can use the affirmative form with 'will' and 'shall'.

ontology.mental_model: Visualizing an action in progress at a point in the future using formal auxiliary
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'shall be -ing' or 'will be -ing' for future ongoing actions.

positives: I shall be attending class the day after tomorrow.
We will be waiting for you at the cafe.
negatives: I shall go to the market later.
I will be happy to assist you.

can_do_statement: Can use the future continuous with 'will' to talk about an event or action in progress at a specified time in the future.

ontology.mental_model: Connecting a future time expression with an ongoing action
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Combine 'Tomorrow' or 'Tonight' with 'will be -ing' for future plans.

positives: Tomorrow I'll be working in the morning.
Tonight we will be resting.
negatives: I'll be working later today.
Tomorrow I will work hard.

can_do_statement: Can use the negative form with 'will' ('won’t').

ontology.mental_model: Expressing that an action will not be in progress at a future time
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'won't be -ing' to say what you will not be doing in the future.

positives: I won't be attending your English class next week.
He will not be coming to the party.
negatives: I will be attending the class.
I won't go there.

can_do_statement: Can use the future continuous with 'will' as a polite question form, in place of the present simple or future simple.

ontology.mental_model: Softening a question by shifting it into a progressive future aspect
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'Will I be -ing?' to ask questions more politely.

positives: Will I be needing any money?
Will you be requiring further assistance today?
negatives: Will they be needing any help?
I will be needing some money.

can_do_statement: Can use the future continuous with 'might' or 'may' to talk about an event or activity potentially in progress at a specified or understood time in the future.

ontology.mental_model: Expressing uncertainty about an action in progress in the future
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'might be -ing' or 'may be -ing' for possible future actions.

positives: The new offerings might be coming up shortly.
Your boss may be calling at 10 pm tonight.
negatives: They will be coming soon.
Your boss may call later.

can_do_statement: Can use 'yes/no' and 'wh-' question forms with 'will'.

ontology.mental_model: Inquiring about an ongoing action in the future
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'Will... be -ing?' to ask about future plans in progress.

positives: Will they be holding any activities at night?
What will you be doing in a few years from now?
negatives: They will be holding activities at night.
Will you do that for me?

can_do_statement: Can use the present forms of 'be' + 'about to'.

ontology.mental_model: Positioning an event on the immediate verge of occurrence
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'am/is/are about to' when something is going to happen very soon.

positives: You are not going to believe what I am about to tell you!
I'm in a hurry, my class is about to begin.
negatives: I was about to begin when the phone rang.
They were about to win the game.

can_do_statement: Can use 'be due to' and, more formally, 'be to' talk about things that are scheduled or expected.

ontology.mental_model: Framing an action as formally scheduled
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'be due to' or 'be to' for scheduled future events.

positives: Our annual conference is due to take place next week.
We are to leave a bit earlier today.
negatives: I was due to go yesterday.
I have to leave right now.

can_do_statement: Can use the present form of 'be' + 'to'.

ontology.mental_model: Framing an action as formally scheduled or required
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'is to' or 'are to' for formal arrangements.

positives: I am to go on a business trip to New York.
He is to come to Athens next Friday.
negatives: I have to go to work.
I am planning to come.

guideword: USE: OBLIGATIONS AND  INSTRUCTIONS WITH 'BE TO'
can_do_statement: Can use 'be to' talk about future obligations and to give instructions.

ontology.mental_model: Imposing an obligation using a formal construction
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'you are to' to give strict instructions.

positives: You're to sit in front of the TV.
They are to have their passports ready.
negatives: They are sitting in front of the TV.
You have to sit here.

guideword: USE: IMMEDIATE FUTURE WITH 'BE ABOUT TO'
can_do_statement: Can use 'be about to' to talk about the immediate future, often with 'just'.

ontology.mental_model: Positioning an event on the immediate verge of occurrence with emphasis
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'just about to' for things happening right this second.

positives: We are just about to launch a new product.
I'm just about to call him.
negatives: We are about to launch a product.
I am just calling him now.

can_do_statement: Can use the present form of 'be' + 'due to'.

ontology.mental_model: Framing an action as formally scheduled using 'due to'
ontology.pedagogical_hook: Use 'is due to' for scheduled events.

positives: I am due to start work in August.
We are due to be present at the meeting.
negatives: I was due to start work last week.
The assignment is due tomorrow.
